text: A new Journals page dated for the current day is created automatically each day
quote: Every day at midnight a new Journals page is created with that day's date, making it easy to see when you've added what information.

text: The app opens on the Journals page every time it launches
quote: Every time you open Logseq, you start on the Journals page.

text: Each journal page shows linked references to that date, so dated mentions work as reminders or TODOs for the future
quote: In the linked references of each day's Journals page you'll see the mentions of that day's date. This is handy for when you want to send your future self reminders or TODOs.

text: Create or reference pages with [[ ]] wiki-style links, or create new pages from the search bar
quote: Type `[[]]` to create or reference any other page. You can also make a new page in the search bar.

text: Reference an individual block from any page using (( )) syntax
quote: Type `[[]]` to create or reference any other page. You can also make a new page in the search bar. Type `(())` to reference a block on any page.

text: Shift-click a reference to open it in the right sidebar, or hover over it to see a preview
quote: Shift-click to open it in the [[Right sidebar]]. Hover over ref to see a preview modal of it.

text: References can be given custom display labels
quote: References can have custom display labels.

text: Top-level blocks can be converted into pages, and back into blocks, by tagging them with #Page
quote: Blocks that have a page as a parent i.e. usually top-level blocks can be converted to a page and back to a block easily. To convert this block to a page, simply tag the block with `#Page`.

text: Simple queries can be written with {{query}} syntax or created with the /query command
quote: Simple queries by using `{{query }}`... You can type `/query` to create a simple query.

text: Queries support a date-range (between start end) filter over journal blocks
quote: The format `(between start end)` will only support blocks on the journal pages.

text: Search, install, update and remove third-party plugins from a built-in Marketplace dashboard
quote: From this dashboard, third-party plugins from the [[Marketplace]], can be searched, installed, updated and removed.

text: Load unpacked plugins that are distributed outside the marketplace
quote: Click on `Load unpacked plugin` to load plugins that are distributed outside the marketplace.

text: Themes are distributed and installed as a type of plugin
quote: Themes are distributed as plugins and are a type of plugin.

text: Documented plugin API with namespaces for App, Editor, DB, Git, UI, Assets and FileStorage
quote: logseq.App logseq.Editor logseq.DB logseq.Git logseq.UI logseq.Assets logseq.FileStorage

text: An optional local HTTP server gives authorized external access to the graph database
quote: we developed the local HTTP server to support external access to the database through authorization.

text: The local API serves its own documentation, exposes a single POST /api endpoint that dispatches plugin API methods, and uses bearer-token auth
quote: The local HTTP API server ships its own API documentation and a single method-dispatch endpoint: "By default, api documentation is available at http://127.0.0.1:12315/."; "POST `/api` - `method` can be any of the ones listed in https://plug

text: The local HTTP API can write content, for example inserting blocks into pages via logseq.Editor.insertBlock
quote: -d '{"method": "logseq.Editor.insertBlock", "args": ["Test page", "This is a new block", {"isPageBlock": true}]}'

text: The logseq:// protocol lets third-party applications invoke actions within Logseq
quote: Logseq provides a protocol `logseq://` to allow third party applications to invoke actions within Logseq.

text: A quick-capture x-callback URL saves short text and links and can be run from a browser bookmark or the command line
quote: Quick capture for short text and links. Can be added as a bookmark link to modern browser or opened from command line shell

text: Quick capture formatting is configurable with templates using variables such as time, text and URL
quote: :quick-capture-templates {:text "[[quick capture]] **{time}**: {text} from {url}"

text: Individual pages can be marked public for publishing with the publish:: true property
quote: Individual pages can be marked as public with the property `publish:: true`.

text: A graph can be published as a web single-page application
quote: This feature publishes a graph as a [[Publish Web]], single page application (SPA).

text: Published sites can read user customization from config.edn, custom.css, custom.js and export.css
quote: Published apps can read user configuration from [[config.edn]], [[custom.css]], [[custom.js]] and [[export.css]].

text: Export data as text, HTML, OPML, PNG, EDN, JSON and standard Markdown
quote: The Logseq Export feature allows users to export their data in various formats, including text, HTML, OPML, PNG, EDN, JSON, and standard Markdown.

text: Export text selections, blocks, individual pages, or the entire graph, with customizable options
quote: It supports exporting text selections, blocks, individual pages, or the entire graph with customizable options.

text: Export the graph in a Roam Research-compatible JSON format
quote: **Roam JSON**: Export the graph in Roam Research compatible format.

text: Spatial whiteboard canvas that combines knowledge-base blocks with shapes, drawings, website embeds and connectors
quote: Put thoughts from your knowledge base as well as new ones next to each other on a spatial canvas together with shapes, drawings, website embeds and connectors.

text: Create a new whiteboard with the n w keyboard shortcut
quote: You can also create a new whiteboard with the keyboard shortcut `n w`.

text: Sync service keeps up to 10 graphs in sync across Desktop, Android and iOS
quote: Syncs up to 10 graphs between Logseq Desktop, Android, and iOS.

text: Synced graphs are end-to-end encrypted
quote: Yes, your graph is end-to-end encrypted.

text: Each synced graph is encrypted with a password, covering both file contents and file names
quote: Each graph is encrypted with a password. The contents of the file as well as its name are all encrypted.

text: Sync encryption is built on Age encryption and ChaCha20-Poly1305
quote: Basic algorithm: [Age Encryption](https://github.com/FiloSottile/age) and [ChaCha20-Poly1305]

text: Sync is opt-in per graph, so some graphs can stay local-only
quote: Syncing is a choice that is made per graph and thus allows for some graphs to be local only.

text: Positioned as a privacy-first, open-source knowledge base
quote: Logseq: A privacy-first, open-source knowledge base

text: Pages and zoomed-in blocks can be added to favorites
quote: Nodes can be favorited. For a zoomed in block, use the `Add to/remove from favorites` command.

text: Zotero integration for document annotation and citations
quote: Learn how to set up Zotero in combination with Logseq, and get access to powerful document annotation and citation features.
